records.evidence_job: Practice breaking down one coherent free-response-style physics situation; interpret the shared representation, use an earlier conclusion in a later part, and make or justify a model/plan choice.
records.student_action: Interpret the shared stimulus, carry evidence forward between connected parts, and justify a physics plan/model choice.
records.student_text:
The diagram shows the geometry used by Eratosthenes: sunlight is nearly parallel, Syene and Alexandria are about 800 km apart, and the measured angle at Alexandria is about 7.1°, close to 1/50 of a full circle. Use the shared diagram for all parts.
(a) Identify the two measured pieces of evidence that connect the two cities in the model.
(b) If 7.1° is about 1/50 of a circle, what fraction of Earth’s circumference does the 800 km separation represent?
(c) Use your conclusion from part (b) to estimate Earth’s circumference.
(d) Explain why this is a testable physics claim rather than a guess. Name one measurement that another group could repeat.
records.student_html:
The diagram shows the geometry used by Eratosthenes: sunlight is nearly parallel, Syene and Alexandria are about 800 km apart, and the measured angle at Alexandria is about 7.1°, close to 1/50 of a full circle. Use the shared diagram for all parts.

(a) Identify the two measured pieces of evidence that connect the two cities in the model.

(b) If 7.1° is about 1/50 of a circle, what fraction of Earth’s circumference does the 800 km separation represent?

(c) Use your conclusion from part (b) to estimate Earth’s circumference.

(d) Explain why this is a testable physics claim rather than a guess. Name one measurement that another group could repeat.
records.answer: (a) 800 km separation and about 7.1° angle; (b) 1/50; (c) about 40,000 km; (d) it depends on repeatable measurable distances/angles.
records.answer_text: (a) 800 km separation and about 7.1° angle; (b) 1/50; (c) about 40,000 km; (d) it depends on repeatable measurable distances/angles.
records.solution_text: The angle is approximately one-fiftieth of a full rotation, so the surface distance is modeled as one-fiftieth of the circumference. Thus C ≈ 50(800 km)=40,000 km. The claim is testable because the distance and shadow angle can be measured again and compared with the prediction.
records.solution_html: The angle is approximately one-fiftieth of a full rotation, so the surface distance is modeled as one-fiftieth of the circumference. Thus C ≈ 50(800 km)=40,000 km. The claim is testable because the distance and shadow angle can be measured again and compared with the prediction.
